title: US supreme court allows Trump officials to resume deportations to third countries
summary:
Conservative majority temporarily lifts lower-court decision as liberal justices dissent from ruling

The Trump administration may deport immigrants to a “third country”, or a country other…

blocks.text: The Trump administration may deport immigrants to a “third country”, or a country other than their homeland, without providing them an opportunity to dispute due to humanitarian concerns, the supreme court said in a brief order on Tuesday.

The six-justice conservative majority of the high court temporarily lifted a lower court decision that determined immigrants being deported to a third country needed notice to argue they are at risk of persecution.
As is typical in emergency orders, the justices did not explain why it granted the administration’s request.
The three liberal justices of the court, Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson, dissented from the ruling.
Tuesday’s ruling will take effect while the supreme court considers the larger question in the case. Justices said they would hear oral arguments in December.
